projectDir.description: Directory holding the project, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.

build-manifest.name: Project has a build manifest
build-manifest.description: The project declares a recognised build manifest, so the build is reproducible and tooling can find it.
build-manifest.remediation: Add a build manifest at the project root: `build.gradle.kts` (Gradle Kotlin DSL), `build.gradle` (Gradle Groovy DSL) or `pom.xml` (Maven). Without one, nobody but the author can build the checkout.

gradle-wrapper.name: Gradle wrapper is committed
gradle-wrapper.description: A Gradle project commits `gradlew` and the wrapper properties that pin the Gradle version.
gradle-wrapper.remediation:
Generate the wrapper and commit every file it writes:

```bash
gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.14
git add gradlew gradlew.bat gradle/wrapper
```

The wrapper pins the Gradle version, so the checkout builds the same way on a laptop and on CI, without installing Gradle first.

kotlin-version-pinned.name: Kotlin version is pinned
kotlin-version-pinned.description: The build declares the Kotlin compiler version, and it is no older than the configured floor.
kotlin-version-pinned.remediation: Declare the compiler version where the build applies the Kotlin plugin. For example, use `kotlin("jvm") version "2.4.0"` in `build.gradle.kts`, a `kotlin` entry under `[versions]` in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, or `<kotlin.version>` in `pom.xml`. Without it, the compiler version can drift between a laptop and CI.

minVersion.description: Oldest Kotlin version accepted. A pinned version below this is a violation.

dependencies-locked.name: Gradle dependencies are locked
dependencies-locked.description: The Gradle build commits the lock files that resolve its dependencies, so the same commit builds from the same versions.
dependencies-locked.remediation:
Turn on locking for every configuration and write the lock files:

```kotlin
dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
}
```

```bash
./gradlew dependencies --write-locks
```

Commit the `gradle.lockfile` files this writes. Without them, a dynamic version, or a transitive dependency whose own range moved, can resolve differently when the same commit is rebuilt, so the build that shipped is not the build that was reviewed.

minLockfiles.description: Fewest lock files the build must commit.
